perf.summary: Russian-peasant O(log b) loop is only needed when a*b can overflow Int64; for small moduli a direct (a*b)%mod is one multiply.
perf.currentCost: Up to ~63 iterations, each with 2 conditional doublings/adds, a branch on the low bit, a shift, and repeated (mod - a)/(mod - result) subexpressions. This runs every single modular multiply, including the inner loop of ModInv/ModDiv and any exponentiation built on it.
perf.proposedChange: Fast-path when the product cannot overflow: after the % mod and sign fixups, if (mod <= 3037000499L) { return (a * b) % mod; } 3037000499^2 < 2^63, so a,b in [0,mod) gives a*b < 2^63 with no overflow. Fall through to the existing peasant loop only when mod exceeds that bound. This collapses the common 32-bit-modulus case from ~60 dependent iterations to a single mul+rem.
perf.rationale: For the overwhelmingly common case of moduli that fit in ~31 bits (e.g. 1e9+7, 998244353), one hardware MUL + one DIV replaces a 60-iteration dependency chain. Removes a long serial dependency that Burst/CPU cannot pipeline.
perf.risk: Threshold must be a named const and provably correct: floor(sqrt(2^63 - 1)) = 3037000499; (3037000499)^2 = 9223372030926249001 < 9223372036854775807, safe. Inputs a,b must already be reduced to [0,mod) (they are, after the existing %/sign fixups). For mod above the threshold, behavior is unchanged. No signed-mod hazard since operands are non-negative at that point.

perf.summary: Recomputed (mod - a) and (mod - result) and the conditional add/sub can be tightened to one subtract-with-correction per branch.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration computes (mod - a) up to twice and (mod - result) up to twice via the ternary, plus a comparison. The expression result = (mod - result <= a) ? result - (mod - a) : result + a hides two subtractions on the taken path.
perf.proposedChange: If the peasant loop is retained (large-mod path), hoist t = mod - a once per iteration and reuse: add step becomes a = (a >= t) ? a - t : a + a; reduce step for result similarly with d = mod - result computed once. Each branch then does at most one subtraction instead of forming (mod - a) twice.
perf.rationale: Cuts redundant subtractions in the hot per-iteration body and shortens the dependency chain, helping the large-modulus path that the overflow-safe fast path does not cover.
perf.risk: Pure arithmetic refactor; operands remain in [0,mod) so all intermediates stay non-negative and within range. Semantics identical. Only relevant on the slow path; keep as named local, not magic recompute.
